candidates.change_summary: Change the block requirement from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2, delaying when settle() can be called.
Change the block requirement from block.number + 1 to block.number, allowing immediate settlement in the same block.
Remove the payment requirement (msg.value == 1 ether), allowing lockInGuess without sending ETH.
Change payment requirement from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Remove the initial require check for guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, allowing overwriting an existing guess.
Delete the first require statement, allowing lockInGuess to be called even if the sender already has a non-zero guess block.
Delete the second require statement, allowing lockInGuess to be called with a msg.value other than exactly 1 ether.
Replace the assignment of the stored guess with assignment of the caller-supplied hash XORed with 1, changing the recorded guess.
Replace the guess-block assignment with block.number + 2, delaying the earliest block at which settle can succeed.
Change the block-number assignment so lockInGuess records the current block number instead of future block.number + 1.
Remove the assignment that stores the submitted guess hash, leaving only the block-number state update.
Remove the assignment that records the lock block number, so a successful call does not change the caller's stored block value.
Change the initial-guess requirement to reject callers whose stored block value is nonzero instead of requiring it to be zero.
Change the payment requirement to reject exactly 1 ether instead of requiring exactly 1 ether.
Change the stored guess assignment so it records the caller address as bytes32 instead of the submitted hash.
Change the lock block assignment to store the caller's guess hash in the block field instead of a future block number.
Change the lock block assignment to store the current timestamp instead of a future block number.
Insert an assignment that clears the caller's stored guess hash after storing it.
Change the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Change the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to 0.
Change the assignment of the guess block from block.number + 1 to 1.
Change the lock check require from guesses[msg.sender].block == 0 to guesses[msg.sender].block != 0.
Change the value payment requirement from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Delete the assignment of the guess hash.
Delete the assignment of the guess block.
Delete the check that the value sent is 1 ether.
Delete the check that the caller has not already locked in a guess.
Insert a write of the guess hash to storage before the lock check.
Insert a write of the guess block to storage before the lock check.
Insert a return statement at the start of the function, skipping all state updates.
Move the block assignment before the hash assignment.
Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` with `guesses[msg.sender].guess = bytes32(0);`, so the stored guess is always zero instead of the provided hash.

Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` with `guesses[msg.sender].guess = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash));`, so the stored guess is a hash of the provided value rather than the value itself.
Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number;`, so the target block number is one less than in the original.
Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 2;`, so the target block number is one greater than in the original.
Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;`, so the guess remains lockable because the stored block stays zero.
Replace the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` with `guesses[msg.sender].block = 1;`, so the stored block is the constant 1 rather than the current block plus one.
Replace the amount check `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` with `require(msg.value >= 1 ether);`, allowing lock-in with more than one ether.
Replace the amount check `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` with `require(msg.value > 1 ether);`, rejecting the exact one-ether payment that the original accepts.
Replace the amount check `require(msg.value == 1 ether);` with `require(msg.value != 1 ether);`, rejecting the exact one-ether payment that the original accepts.
Replace the re-lock guard `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);` with `require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0);`, allowing only addresses that have already locked in to call again.
Replace the re-lock guard `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);` with `require(guesses[msg.sender].guess == 0);`, checking the guess field instead of the block field before locking in.
Delete the re-lock guard `require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0);`, allowing an address to call lockInGuess multiple times and overwrite its guess and target block.
Delete the payment check `require(msg.value == 1 ether);`, allowing an address to lock in a guess without sending any ether.
Delete the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;`, so calling lockInGuess updates the target block but leaves the stored guess unchanged (zero for first-time callers).
Delete the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;`, so the target block stays zero and the caller remains eligible to lock in again.
Move the assignment `guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1;` before `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;`, so the target block is recorded first and the guess second.
Change the lock block from block.number + 1 to block.number, so the recorded block differs by one.
Change the lock block to block.number + 2, so the recorded block differs by one.
Remove the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash, so the stored guess hash is not updated.
Store the provided hash value negated via bitwise NOT, changing the stored guess bytes.
Remove the require that the sender has not already locked a guess, allowing relocking and changing subsequent recorded state.
Change the stored guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the stored guess block from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Change the stored guess hash to keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash)).
Change the stored guess hash to bytes32(uint256(hash) + 1).
Change the first require to check that the sender has not already stored a zero guess.
Change the non-zero block guard to always require false.
Change the payment amount requirement from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Change the payment amount requirement from 1 ether to 0 ether.
Delete the first require guard.
Delete the payment amount require guard.
Delete the state update that stores the guess hash.
Delete the state update that stores the guess block.
Move the payment amount require after the guess hash assignment.
Move the payment amount require after the guess block assignment.
Move the guess block assignment before the guess hash assignment.
Replace the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].guess with an assignment of the keccak256 hash of the input hash.
Replace the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].block with a constant block number of 1, breaking the intended future-block settlement condition.
Replace the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].block with block.number, removing the +1 and allowing same-block settlement.
Insert a statement that assigns block.number to guesses[msg.sender].block before setting it to block.number + 1, temporarily altering the stored block value during execution.
Delete the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].block, leaving the stored block as zero and allowing repeated lock-ins.
Replace the check requiring a zero prior guess block with a check on the sender's guess field, changing the lock-in eligibility condition.
Replace the payable amount check with a check for zero msg.value, so nonpayable calls can pass the guard and update state.
Replace the payable amount check with a looser non-zero check, accepting any positive value instead of exactly one ether.
Move the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].block before the assignment of guesses[msg.sender].guess, changing the intermediate state order during execution.
Replace the forwarded guess hash with a hash of the sender address, changing the stored guess to something independent of the caller-supplied hash.
Replace the stored guess assignment with the zero hash, making every lock-in store the same default value.
Replaced the guess hash assignment to store the previous stored guess instead of the function argument.
Replaced the lock block assignment to use the current block number instead of the next block number.
Replaced the lock block assignment to use the previous block number instead of the next block number.
Inserted an additional assignment that doubles the lock block offset to block.number + 2.
Deleted the assignment that records the caller's guess hash.
Deleted the assignment that marks the guess as locked at a future block.
Replaced the zero-block guard with a guard that requires the lock block to be nonzero.
Replaced the one-ether payment guard with a guard that requires exactly two ether.
Moved the guess hash assignment to after the lock block assignment.
Moved the one-ether payment guard to after the state updates.
Change the stored guess value from the provided hash to the zero hash, so lockInGuess always records bytes32(0).
Store the current block number in the guess field instead of the provided hash, so lockInGuess records block.number as the guess.
Set the stored block height to the current block number instead of block.number + 1, making the guess immediately settleable on the next block if that block matches.
Set the stored block height to block.number + 2 instead of block.number + 1, delaying the earliest possible settlement by one block.
Remove the requirement that no prior guess exists, so a sender can lock in a new guess and overwrite an existing block height.
Remove the one ether payment requirement, so lockInGuess can be called without sending exactly 1 ether.
Delete the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].block, so the guess is recorded but no block height is stored.
Delete the assignment to guesses[msg.sender].guess, so the block height is recorded but the guess hash is not stored.
Remove the requirement that the guess matches the answer, always sending 2 ether if block check passes.
Change the equality check to inequality so payout occurs when guess does NOT match answer.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Delete the guessing block number update, leaving guesses[msg.sender].block unchanged so subsequent settles still see the guess.
Replace the block.number check with block.number >= (instead of >) so settle can be called in the same block.
Replace the blockhash input to use block.number - 1 instead of the stored block, changing the answer.
Change the second precondition to require block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block instead of strictly greater.
Change the first precondition to require guesses[msg.sender].block == 0.
Change the answer hash to use the current blockhash instead of the stored guess blockhash.
Delete the state update that resets the guess block to zero.
Change the payout balance precondition to require at least 1 ether instead of 2 ether.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Replace the first settle require checks with a no-op condition that always passes.
Delete the require that the sender has locked in a guess.
Change the timing check from strictly greater than to greater-or-equal.
Use the current block hash in the answer instead of the committed block's hash.
Move the guess reset to after the payout transfer, making it a pre-call state update.
Check for a sufficiently small balance instead of the required 2 ether payout amount.
Transfer only 1 ether to the winner instead of the original 2 ether.
Change the win condition so settle never pays out even when the guess matches the answer.
Delete the payout transfer so a correct guess never receives funds.
Change the balance requirement from 2 ether to 3 ether, preventing payout when only 2 ether is available.
Replace the answer hash with a computation from the current block's blockhash, changing when the guess matches.
Change the maturity check to allow settling in the same block as the guess by using >= instead of >.
Changed the comparison from == to !=, so the payout condition is inverted.
Changed the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering the observable transfer value on a successful settle.
Changed the balance requirement from 2 ether to 1 ether, altering when a successful settle can pay out.
Changed the timing guard from strictly greater than to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settle earlier than intended.
Changed the blockhash source to the current block number, altering the answer computation and thus payout eligibility.
Change the settle block-number guard from strictly greater than the stored block to strictly less than it.
Change the settle block-number guard to require the current block be greater than or equal to the stored block instead of strictly greater.
Change the settle block-number guard to require the current block be less than or equal to the stored block instead of strictly greater.
Change the settle block-number guard to require the current block be greater than or equal to 0 instead of greater than the stored block.
Change the answer hash input from the stored block hash to the current block hash.
Change the answer hash input from the stored block hash to the zero block hash.
Change the answer hash input to use the stored user guess instead of the block hash.
Change the payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the payout balance precondition from at least 2 ether to at least 1 ether.
Change the stored block reset value from 0 to 1.
Delete the statement that resets the stored block to 0.
Require block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block instead of strictly greater, allowing settlement within the locked block.
Use the current blockhash instead of the stored guess block's blockhash.
Transfer the entire contract balance instead of exactly 2 ether when the guess is correct.
Compare the hash of the sender with the answer instead of the stored guess.
Lower the payout balance requirement from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Use the entire contract balance in the keccak256 preimage instead of the target block's hash.
Use the sender's address in the keccak256 preimage instead of the target block's hash.
Use the current block number in the keccak256 preimage instead of the target block's hash.
Insert an unconditional transfer of 2 ether to the sender before the correct-guess check.
Delete the requirement that the target block has passed before settling.
Delete the requirement that the sender has an outstanding guess before settling.
Delete the payout balance requirement.
Delete the reset of the sender's guess block to zero.
Replace the strict block-number check with a non-strict one, allowing settle in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Change the answer source from the recorded block hash to the current block hash.
Change the payout comparison to always compare against a zero answer instead of the computed hash.
Delete the reset of the caller's guess block before settlement.
Replace the strict block-number check with a non-strict one, allowing settlement in the same block as the recorded guess block.
Remove the requirement that the caller has a nonzero guess block, allowing settlement attempts without locking in a guess.
Change the answer computation to hash the caller-provided guess instead of the recorded block hash.
Change the payout comparison to always succeed by comparing the answer to itself.
Increase the payout amount from 2 ether to 3 ether.
Change the balance guard to require at least 1 ether instead of 2 ether.
Change the answer computation to use the current block hash instead of the recorded guess block hash.
Change the answer computation to use the previous block hash relative to the current block.
Change the settle payout from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the settle answer hash input from the block hash to the current block hash.
Change the settle win condition from equality to inequality.
Change the settle time check to require the current block is not past the guess block.
Delete the require that the guess block is nonzero, allowing settle to proceed for callers who never locked in a guess.
Replace the strict block-number wait requirement with a non-strict comparison, letting settle succeed at the same block as the recorded guess block.
Replace the answer hash input from the stored guess block to the current block, changing which blockhash is compared against the guess.
Change the payout threshold check to require only at least 1 ether instead of 2 ether.
Change the successful-guess payout from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Invert the successful-guess condition so payout occurs when the guess does not match the answer.
Delete the state update that clears the guess block after settle, allowing repeated settlement attempts.
